title: Taytu Betul
summary: Taytu Betul, born probably in 1850 or 1851, married Menelik in 1883 and became empress of Ethiopia when he took the imperial throne in 1889. She chose the site of the new capital, Addis Ababa, in 1886. At Adwa on 1 March 1896 she is recorded as organizing the defence perimeter, leading 5,000 men and gathering 10,000 to 12,000 women to carry water and tend the wounded. She died in Addis Ababa in 1918.

uncertainty.note: Birth year is not recorded: Encyclopedia.com says "probably in 1850 or 1851"; the date on her tomb (Ethiopian calendar 1832, i.e. 1839-1840) is called probably not correct by History of Royal Women. Death date is given as February 11, 1918 by Encyclopedia.com and 11 February 1918 by History of Royal Women.

importance.justification: Both sources credit her with choosing the site of Addis Ababa and with a leading support role at Adwa on 1 March 1896; Encyclopedia.com records her as empress from 1889.
